caveats: The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and the independent native-local build-core run reproduced the a5200_libretro.zip package, resolver metadata, both ABI artifacts, and both active-marker build logs byte for byte. Execution was local; both builds cloned the pinned source over the network, so no offline source cache is proven.

The armhf artifact has no libstdc++ dependency, so it clears every captured provider ceiling; ARM64 is bound to ra64-universal-v1 and ARMHF to ra32-a30-v1. Provider inspection and target-runtime capture are absent, so every device view remains provisional and ineligible pending a runtime smoke result.

Content, BIOS/firmware handling, controls, audio/video pacing, saves and state round trips, reset and unload behavior, frontend integration, compatibility, licensing review, and sustained performance remain target-runtime and human gates. Publication remains disabled regardless of local byte reproducibility.

The publication-disabled simulated-Actions build-core run and independent native-local build-core run reproduced both ABI artifacts, resolver metadata, warning-free build logs, and the package byte for byte. The selected github-actions/simulated/local-docker and reproduction local/native/local-docker identities remain explicit; record hashes differ only because timestamps, runner identity, run paths, and run IDs are evidence-bearing fields.

The pristine source is commit 23c1ea482afb08656ec507e9ce98ed242a20bdfa, tree bd8a0b3f925ab9dcd5acae4f705e4f0c00f787b5, with no submodules. Commit-derived GIT_VERSION '-23c1ea4' is bound to all 36 C compiles per ABI and the exact 36-object final link; both binaries report '2.0.2 -23c1ea4', matching resolver display version 2.0.2.

ARM64 requires GLIBC_2.17 and records the AArch64 loader, libc, and libm. ARMHF is EABI5 hard-float, reaches GLIBC_2.7, and records only libc and libm. Neither shared object has a PT_INTERP; loader, rootfs, frontend, and target execution remain runtime gates.
Resolver metadata declares GPLv2; any public distribution or release remains a human legal/policy and corresponding-source gate even though local builds reproduce.

Atari 5200 a52/bin loading, analog joystick and keypad mappings, per-game input hacks, audio/video pacing, saves, deterministic states, cartridge compatibility, and sustained performance remain target-runtime gates. The low-powered-hardware description is not device-performance evidence.

Resolver metadata marks 5200.rom optional and no BIOS is packaged. The binary falls back to its internal Altirra OS but identifies that fallback as reduced-compatibility and recommends the official BIOS; BIOS discovery and compatibility should therefore be tested both with the internal fallback and a separately supplied lawful 5200.rom.

The software-only Unix recipe produces one shared artifact per ABI/build profile and provides no basis for device-specific duplicate builds. ARM64 is build-identity-bound only to ra64-universal-v1, while ARMHF is bound only to ra32-a30-v1. Its modest ARMHF GLIBC floor makes ra32-mini-v0 and ra32-universal-v0 plausible candidates, but provider/build-identity/frontend/runtime capture is still absent; all device views remain ineligible.
